A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HumanOmni-Speaker, with corresponding sections, equations, tables and figures that support reliable comparison. All 13 pages of v2 and 18 pages of v3 were inspected. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, speech-recognition results and encoder/hyperparameter ablations in Tables 2–5 and Figure 6.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds annotation-agreement statistics, error diagnostics, a cropping comparison and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same dual-stream architecture, ResNet-18/SVT/Transformer Visual Delta Encoder, 25 fps sampling, six tokens per frame and three-stage training procedure. The new face-cropped variant is an experimental control, not a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The training sources, five HumanOmni-Speaker benchmark tasks, and LRS2/LRS3 and LibriSpeech evaluations are retained. Added benchmark statistics, speaker-count diagnostics and cropping controls concern existing coverage rather than new datasets or task populations.

E2.justification: Section 7 adds an evaluated alternative using face crops from an unnamed off-the-shelf detector, reporting 38% SI-Hard error versus approximately 21% with full frames. Comparator membership in Tables 2–5 is unchanged; the Whisper-diarization plus Qwen3-VL pipeline already appeared in v2.

E3.justification: Table 2 replaces the combined AVG with separate Atomic AVG and Holistic AVG, changing score aggregation while retaining individual task metrics. Added experiments introduce face-cropped inputs and encoder-on/off profiling on a 5.7-second, 420 × 756 clip using Qwen2.5-Omni-3B on a V100.

E4.justification: V3 adds targeted checks: a residual-SA-WER breakdown and two-versus-three-speaker analysis in Section 6.1, plus a face-cropping control and single-clip computational profiling in Section 7. The existing component, pipeline and token/FPS ablations remain. These are limited extensions within the retained evaluation suite.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 newly reports inter-annotator agreement using Fleiss’ kappa of 0.82 on approximately 1,500 samples, alongside 18% disagreements resolved by adjudication. V2 reported calibration without these statistics. Neither version reports model-performance confidence intervals or repeated-run/seed information.

E6.justification: Individual task scores in Tables 2–5 and Figure 6 remain unchanged. New results include 38% cropped-input SI-Hard error, 21.0% speaker-blind WER, error-component estimates and computational measurements, including 2.62 versus 3.13 seconds without/with delta tokens. Table 2 replaces HumanOmni-Speaker’s overall 16.2 average with atomic/holistic averages of 7.6/37.8; this is new aggregation, not improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The VR-SDR task definition and identity-fixed SA-WER and IER equations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 adds no substantive derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark, Visual Delta Encoder and speaker-centric model contributions, including native lip-reading/localization and comparative-performance claims. Replacing 'shatter this illusion' with 'address this limitation' changes rhetoric rather than scientific scope.

C2.justification: V3 interprets its new diagnostics as identifying cross-modal identity binding as the primary bottleneck and overlapping speech as a remaining challenge. It also attributes cropping degradation to detector errors and lost scene context, and discusses measured computational tradeoffs. These add substantive explanations and qualifications absent from v2.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project repository pointer, benchmark durations and person/speaker statistics, annotation qualifications and adjudication details, explicit Easy/Hard criteria, and profiling hardware/input specifications. It also removes the explicit baseline repository URL and the sentence explaining delta-only isolation in token/FPS ablations. The retained release-upon-acceptance promise does not establish artifact availability.

R1.justification: The same 41 cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. References are reordered and reformatted, with bibliographic metadata changes rather than additions or removals of research.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence remain intact. V3 locally reorganizes Section 7 into named themes, expands the annotation and remaining-challenges discussions, softens two rhetorical phrases, and revises author/affiliation information while adding keywords and contact details.

P2.justification: V3 retypesets the entire document with narrower text blocks, different typography, running headers and resized/repositioned figures and tables. Table 1 gains benchmark-statistics columns, and Table 2 separates atomic and holistic averages. All six figure images themselves are identical; the substantial change is document-wide layout and table presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves transparency through annotation-agreement reporting, separated task aggregates, and new cropping, error and computational checks. These provide evidence and qualifications missing from v2 without changing headline task scores. Benefits remain limited by the unnamed cropping detector, unquantified speaker-count trend and single-clip profiling; the rewrite also loses explicit ablation-isolation detail.
